name: Speedb
tagline: RocksDB-compatible storage engine fork; open-source development stopped after Redis bought it in 2024.
description: Speedb was an Israeli startup's drop-in replacement for RocksDB that rewrote parts of the engine (a new memtable, a sorted hash index, smarter flow control and write delays) to cut write stalls and improve performance on large datasets. It was open-sourced in 2022 under Apache-2.0 and became the storage engine behind Redis Enterprise's auto-tiering. Redis acquired Speedb in March 2024; the public repository has had no commits since June 2024 and the project website no longer responds. Existing users should plan to move back to upstream RocksDB.
statusNote: Acquired by Redis in March 2024; the open-source repo has been inactive since June 2024 (last release 2.8.0, Jan 2024). Move to upstream RocksDB.
strengths: API- and file-compatible with RocksDB for drop-in testing
Reduced write stalls via improved flow control
Sorted hash memtable improved write-heavy performance
weaknesses: No maintenance or security fixes since mid-2024
Falls further behind upstream RocksDB with each release
Vendor website and community channels are gone
useCases: Existing deployments pending migration to RocksDB
Benchmarking write-stall behaviour against upstream RocksDB
